_comment: Demographic model (DESIGN §4.1). Cohort model: population per settlement/unit is counts by sex × age band. All values are Omer-approved STARTING VALUES for tuning (2026-11-04) — deliberately faster than medieval reality. Yearly update runs in December (turn month index 11); hunger acts monthly.
_birthsComment: Session 22, Omer 2026-11-09: births x1.5 (0.18 -> 0.27) so a realm visibly grows within a 400-turn game of seasons. Four modifiers act on top, all below: famine (famineBirthExponent), the granary / surplus factor (granaryBrake: thin stock lowers, a surplus raises), labour (labourBoost: unfilled jobs raise) and crowding (idle hands lower, villages only). On the old 12-turn year a village of 900 took ~30 years to reach the 1,500 town gate.
_famineComment: DECIDED by Omer 2026-11-09: famine drops births significantly until there is enough food for everyone. Births are multiplied by (the year's food sufficiency, 0-1) to this power: 0.9 fed -> 73 %, 0.7 -> 34 %, 0.5 -> 12.5 %. (Was the sufficiency itself, exponent 1.) Reckoned from the year's average, so a settlement is back to full births the first year it is fed.

labourBoost._comment: DECIDED by Omer 2026-11-09 (values draft): missing hands raise births. The share of the settlement's jobs (buildings, fields, the building site) that it has no hands for, at the December reckoning, scales births by 1 + maxBoost x min(1, share / vacancyFull). Idle hands lower births through the crowding rule below (villages), so the two pull a village toward full employment.

_crowdingComment: DECIDED by Omer 2026-11-04 (value 1.0 is a draft for tuning): in the listed tiers, births are multiplied by (1 − penalty × idle share of hands). 0 = off. At 1.0 a village with 30 % of its hands idle has 30 % fewer births — land-starved villages stop growing instead of starving. Towns and cities are excluded: their idle hands are the workshop/recruit pool, not crowding.

granaryBrake._comment: DECIDED by Omer 2026-11-05 (thin side); extended 2026-11-09 (Session 22) to a surplus factor for every tier. The measure is SPARE months = months of stock minus the months until the next harvest (9 in December). spare <= spareEmpty (it will not reach the harvest) -> minFactor; spareFull -> 1; spare >= spareMax -> maxFactor; linear between. A thin granary breeds less (a city stops growing BEFORE famine). Session 22 moved the thresholds from 0 / 4 to 1.5 / 7 months: with births x1.5 a city otherwise overshoots its land and starves in bad harvests (hunger deaths over 40 years of the start position: ~10-25k at 0 / 4, ~1.5-5.5k at 1.5 / 7; ~2.8k before the x1.5); a full one breeds more (this replaces the old flat plentyBirthMultiplier, which only fired above a year of stock). Applies to the listed tiers.

hunger._comment: Extra deaths in a month with an empty granary = shortfall fraction × rate × population; vulnerable bands weighted double.

migration._comment: DESIGN §4.1: when a settlement forecasts that stock + monthly income − consumption will fall below triggerSafetyMonths of consumption before the next harvest arrives, and it has idle hands, this share of idle hands leaves each month, with dependants (proportional slice of all cohorts), for the parent settlement. Omer 2026-11-04: forecast trigger replaces the flat 3-month trigger.

trickle._comment: The PULL FACTOR (DESIGN §4.1, DECIDED by Omer 2026-11-05, Session 11; condition REVISED by Omer in Session 11b). The countryside feeds the town people as well as grain. Once a year (December) a settlement whose idle hands exceed minIdleShare of its hands sends sharePerYear of its idle hands, with dependants, to its parent — but only if the parent is PROSPEROUS: fully fed that year (requireFedParent) and fed with margin (requireProsperous: its spare months at the next harvest — December stock in months minus the 9 months to September, the granary brake's measure — are at least prosperousSpareMonths). People moved to towns because towns were prosperous, not because the crown had a job open (the Session 11 'vacancies' condition never fired and was dropped). spread randomizes the share by ±spread (0.5 → 50 %–150 % of sharePerYear). sharePerYear 0 turns it off.

noise._comment: DECIDED by Omer 2026-11-05 (sampling adopted; epidemics adopted for now — natural events will become a game-wide mechanic later). vitalSampling 1 = births and deaths are drawn as Poisson counts around the expected value (variance = mean, so villages jitter and cities barely move); 0 = exact fractions (the deterministic model). epidemic: each settlement each year has chancePerYear of an epidemic year in which deaths are multiplied by deathMultiplier; chance 0 turns it off. All draws come from the seeded game RNG, so a game still replays identically.

startingDistribution._comment: Shares used to create a settlement of N people; roughly stationary for the rates above. Men/women split 50/50 within each band.
